viewContainer.title: Open DB Client
welcome.connections:
No database connections yet.

Before connecting you need a JDBC driver jar. Open the driver folder and drop the jar in, then add a connection.

[Add Connection](command:open-dbclient.addConnection)
[Open Driver Folder](command:open-dbclient.openDriverFolder)

config.title: Open DB Client
config.javaHome.description: Path to the Java installation used for the JDBC bridge. Leave empty to auto-detect from `JAVA_HOME` or `PATH`. Requires **Java 17 or newer**.
config.javaArgs.description: Extra JVM arguments appended to the bridge command line, e.g. `--add-opens=java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED`. Useful for legacy JDBC drivers that need reflective access on Java 17+.
config.jvmMaxHeap.description: Maximum heap for the JDBC bridge process (equivalent to `-Xmx`). Defaults to `1g`.
config.driverPaths.description: Extra locations to look for JDBC driver jars. Each entry may be a folder (scanned for `.jar` files directly inside it, not recursively) or a jar file itself. The folder managed by `DB Client: Add Driver Jar` is always scanned, so this is only needed for jars kept elsewhere.
config.driverClassNames.description: Driver classes to load explicitly, in addition to those jars advertise through `META-INF/services/java.sql.Driver`. Needed only for drivers that omit that file; without it such a driver cannot be loaded at all. Example: `com.vendor.jdbc.VendorDriver`.
config.poolSize.description: Maximum number of pooled JDBC connections per profile. The default of `1` behaves like a single long-lived connection, which suits interactive use. Raise it only if you run queries concurrently.
config.fetchSize.description: Rows transferred per fetch when browsing a result grid.
config.confirmDangerous.description: Ask for confirmation before running statements that look destructive (`DROP`, `TRUNCATE`, `DELETE`/`UPDATE` without a `WHERE` clause).
config.maxRows.description: Row ceiling applied to every statement run from an editor. A statement that hits the ceiling is reported as truncated rather than silently cut short. Set to `0` for no ceiling. This does not affect exports, which are unbounded by design.
config.codeLens.description: Show a Run action above every statement in a SQL file.
config.resultOpenIn.below: Split the editor downwards, so the result sits under the SQL (up/down).
config.resultOpenIn.beside: Split the editor to the right, so the result sits next to the SQL (left/right).
config.variablePattern.description: Regular expression that finds a parameter in a SQL script, with one capture group for its name. The default matches `${V_DATE}`. Matching text with no capture group is used whole as the name. Values are substituted before the statement runs; a placeholder with no value stops the run rather than being replaced by an empty string.
config.ddlQueries.description:
Ask the database for a table's DDL instead of reconstructing it from JDBC metadata. Many databases answer this directly and better: `SHOW CREATE TABLE` on MySQL, `DESC` on Hive, `pg_get_tabledef` on PostgreSQL. Those statements are dialect-specific, so they are yours to write.

The **first rule whose `match` fits the connection's JDBC URL wins**; `*` matches any characters and the whole URL must match. A rule with no `match` fits every connection, so put it last to use it as a fallback. With no matching rule the built-in generator runs, which is what keeps the default behaviour unchanged.

A template may use `${table}`, `${schema}`, `${catalog}`, `${qualified}`, `${column}` and `${connectionName}` for the **names as the driver reported them**, or `${quotedTable}`, `${quotedSchema}`, `${quotedCatalog}`, `${quotedQualified}` and `${quotedColumn}` for the same names wrapped in the database's quoting character. Use the unquoted forms in a string literal - `pg_get_tabledef('${qualified}')` - and the quoted ones where an identifier is expected.

The result is shown as the database returned it: one cell becomes a document, anything else opens in the result grid. The `ddl.ifNotExists`, `ddl.indent`, `ddl.includeIndexes` and `ddl.quoteIdentifiers` settings apply only to the built-in generator, so they are ignored when a rule matches.
config.ddlQueries.id: Optional name for the rule, used in messages.
config.ddlQueries.match: Glob tested against the JDBC URL, e.g. jdbc:hive2:*. Omit to match every connection.
config.ddlQueries.sql: The statement to run, with optional ${...} placeholders.
config.ddlIfNotExists.description: Generate `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` rather than `CREATE TABLE`.
config.ddlIndent.description: Indent used for each generated column definition. Spaces, a tab or nothing at all.
config.ddlIncludeIndexes.description: Append `CREATE INDEX` statements after the table. Turn off when indexes are managed separately from table definitions.
config.ddlQuoteIdentifiers.description: Quote identifiers with the character the database itself reports. Turn off for a plain, unquoted name.
config.actions.description:
Your own SQL actions, offered on tables, views and columns in the connection tree. Reachable from the play icon on a node, or from the command palette.

A template may use `${table}`, `${schema}`, `${catalog}`, `${qualified}`, `${column}` and `${connectionName}` for the **names as the driver reported them**, or `${quotedTable}`, `${quotedSchema}`, `${quotedCatalog}`, `${quotedQualified}` and `${quotedColumn}` for the same names wrapped in the database's quoting character. Use the quoted forms where an identifier is expected - `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ${quotedQualified}` - and the unquoted ones inside a string literal.

A placeholder that cannot be filled for the node - `${column}` on a table, say - stops the action instead of being replaced by nothing, because `LIKE '%${column}%'` expanding to `LIKE '%%'` would quietly match everything.

The statement opens in a bound editor rather than running invisibly, so you can see it, change it, and run it again.
config.actions.id: Stable identifier, shown next to the label in the picker.
config.actions.label: What the action is called.
config.actions.descriptionField: Optional: shown as the action's description in the picker.
config.actions.appliesTo: Where the action is offered. Omit to offer it everywhere.
config.resultMaxCacheBytes.description: Maximum disk space (in bytes) the bridge may use for cached result sets. Least-recently-used results are evicted beyond this limit. Defaults to 512 MiB.
config.intellisenseEnabled.description: Enable SQL completion for tables, views, schemas, columns and keywords.
config.intellisensePrefetchTables.descri: Prefetch table names in the background right after connecting, so the first completion is instant. Disable this if your database has thousands of tables and connecting feels slow.
config.intellisenseColumnCacheLimit.desc: How many tables to keep column metadata for in the completion cache (LRU). Lower this to reduce memory on very large databases.
config.healthEnabled.description: Collect JDBC bridge health metrics (JVM memory, GC, pool, result cache, query statistics).
config.healthRefreshInterval.description: How often the bridge pushes health metrics, in milliseconds.
config.healthShowStatusBar.description: Show a health summary in the status bar.
config.csvDelimiter.description: Field separator for CSV export. Any text up to 8 characters: `,`, `;`, a tab, or something the data cannot contain such as `~@~`. The export dialog asks for it and offers the common ones.
config.csvQuoting.description: How fields are quoted in CSV export. `minimal` quotes a field only when it would otherwise be misread, `always` quotes every field, and `never` writes fields as they are - which makes a smaller, plainer file that can no longer be parsed if a value contains the separator.
config.csvWriteBom.description: Write a UTF-8 BOM so Excel detects the encoding correctly. Turn off for tools that choke on a BOM.
config.excelMaxRowsPerSheet.description: Row limit per Excel worksheet; further rows spill into additional sheets.
config.includeHeader.description: Include a header row in CSV and Excel exports.
config.useColumnRemarks.description: Use a column's comment (the name it is documented under, often a Chinese label) as its header when the driver reports one, in both the result grid and exports. Turn off to always show the physical column name.
config.logLevel.description: Verbosity of the "DB Client" output channel and the bridge process log.
